documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M here to set himself up with us; prior office records in chart.

CC: establish care, no acute issues.

HPI: Long history of gallstone pancreatitis that turned chronic. Takes Creon 36,000 with every meal and snack, says when he skips it he knows within an hour (greasy stools, cramping). Has not had a flare needing the hospital in a couple of years. Gallbladder is still in. Not sure why nobody took it out, says it came up once and he was busy. Omeprazole every morning. Told years ago he has a floppy mitral valve, knows his father has the same thing. Takes baby aspirin because a prior doctor told him to. No chest pain, palpitations, syncope. Climbs ladders and walks job sites all day without trouble.

PMH: as above. No surgeries.
Meds: pancrelipase 36,000 units lipase with meals/snacks, ASA 81 daily, omeprazole 20 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MVP. Mother had gallstones. Uncle on mom's side has chronic pancreatitis.
SH: site supervisor for a commercial builder. Smoked about 12 pack-years, stopped at 42. 3-4 beers a week, no binge. Lives alone in Amherst. Rides a motorcycle in season.

ROS: weight stable, no abdominal pain currently, no steatorrhea on enzymes, no dyspnea, no edema.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 34. Pleasant, well appearing. Oropharynx clear, teeth in decent repair. Neck supple. Heart regular, mid-systolic click with a soft late systolic murmur at the apex, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, nontender, no masses. No edema. Skin without rash.

A/P:
1. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis, on enzymes - stable. Continue Creon, omeprazole. CMP today. Will revisit whether surgery should look at the gallbladder once I know him better.
2. MVP with mild MR - exam matches. Continue aspirin as he has been.
3. Obesity, BMI 34 - talked briefly about food and activity, he is not interested in medication now.
4. Former smoker - 12 pk-yr, does not meet lung screening.
5. Health maintenance: flu shot today. Hep C and HIV screening today. Lipids, A1c. Colon screening due - we will set up a FIT at his physical in the spring, he prefers that to colonoscopy.

RTC spring for physical, sooner prn. Gave him my cell.

documents.body: Brett, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver numbers, sugar and cholesterol all where they should be, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Nothing to change. See you in the spring.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Orthopedic Surgery
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, orthopaedic trauma service
Admitted 12/02/2024, discharged 12/07/2024

Diagnosis: closed right femoral shaft fracture, motorcycle collision.
Procedure 12/02/2024: open reduction and internal fixation, right femoral shaft.

Presentation: 45-year-old man brought in after a motorcycle collision with severe right thigh pain, obvious deformity, unable to stand. Alert and oriented, hemodynamically stable, in considerable pain. Imaging confirmed a right femoral shaft fracture. No other injuries identified on trauma survey. Taken to the OR the same evening.

Anesthesia event: rapid sequence intubation with propofol and succinylcholine. Fasciculations of the face and chest were seen within seconds, followed by complete paralysis as expected. Fixation proceeded uneventfully. However, more than an hour after anesthetic agents were stopped, the patient had no spontaneous respiratory effort and no movement. Vital signs remained stable throughout. Repeat neurologic examination showed flaccid paralysis that was not explained by residual sedation. The anesthesia team felt this pointed to an underlying metabolic or genetic cause and suspected plasma (pseudo)cholinesterase deficiency. He was kept intubated, sedated and ventilated in recovery until neuromuscular function returned, and was extubated that night without difficulty. Plasma cholinesterase activity and dibucaine number were sent 12/04; results will be forwarded by the anesthesia department.

Hospital course: pain controlled on oral regimen. Albumin 2.9 on 12/03, noted as hypoalbuminemia; diet advanced, enzymes resumed with meals. Mobilized with PT, walker, weight bearing as tolerated on the right. Enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis.

Home medications continued: pancrelipase with meals and snacks, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.
New: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, 1-2 tabs q6h prn; enoxaparin 40 mg subcut daily x 28 days.
Allergies: NKDA on admission. Anesthesia alert: prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine - avoid pending results.

Follow-up: orthopaedics clinic 2 weeks, outpatient PT, primary care within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge from regional hospital (R femur ORIF 12/2). Home, getting around with walker. Pain moderate, taking oxycodone-APAP about 3x/day. Doing his own enoxaparin shots, no bleeding. Eating, taking Creon. Bowels slow, suggested OTC senna. No fever, no calf pain, no SOB. TCM visit booked Thu 12/12 - he has a ride.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 10 days after a motorcycle crash: closed R femoral shaft fracture, ORIF 12/2 at the regional hospital, home 12/7. Discharge summary reviewed.

The anesthesia part is the bigger issue long term. He got succinylcholine for RSI and stayed paralyzed well over an hour after the case, kept on the vent until it wore off, extubated that night. Anesthesia suspects pseudocholinesterase deficiency and sent levels; not back yet. He remembers nothing of it, was told about it the next morning. Also albumin 2.9 inpatient.

Now: walking with walker, WBAT. Pain improving, oxycodone-APAP 2-3 a day. Enoxaparin daily, no bruising beyond injection sites. Eating ok, Creon with meals. Constipated, senna helping.

Meds: pancrelipase w/ meals and snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, oxycodone-APAP 5/325 prn, enoxaparin 40 daily through ~12/30.
Allergies: NKDA; succinylcholine reaction pending workup.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Uncomfortable getting onto the table but ok. Heart regular with his usual click/soft apical murmur. Lungs clear. R lateral thigh incision clean, dry, staples in, no erythema. Calves soft, nontender. Distal pulses intact, sensation intact.

A/P:
1. R femoral shaft fracture s/p ORIF - healing course per ortho, f/u 12/23. PT started. Taper oxycodone as able; no refill planned.
2. VTE prophylaxis - finish 28 days enoxaparin.
3. Prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine - await cholinesterase results. Flagged in chart now as an anesthesia alert.
4. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today. Push protein, keep enzymes with every meal and snack.
5. Work - off duty until cleared by ortho; note given.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brett - your blood counts are fine and kidneys are fine. Albumin (a protein made by the liver that drops when you're sick or not absorbing food well) is 3.1, a little better than in the hospital but still low. Keep the Creon with every meal and snack and aim for protein at each meal - eggs, chicken, Greek yogurt, a shake if you're not hungry. We'll recheck it in the spring.

allergies.reaction: Prolonged paralysis and apnea after anesthesia

documents.title: Letter from Department of Anesthesiology
documents.author: anesthesiology
documents.body:
Re: Brett Coughlin, DOB 05/24/1979

Dear Doctor,

Your patient had prolonged neuromuscular blockade after succinylcholine during emergency fixation of a right femoral shaft fracture on 12/02/2024, requiring postoperative ventilation for several hours. Plasma cholinesterase testing drawn 12/04/2024 has resulted:

Plasma cholinesterase activity: 1,850 U/L (reference 5,320-12,920)
Dibucaine number: 21 (reference 79-87)

The low activity with a markedly reduced dibucaine number is the pattern of the homozygous atypical variant, i.e. inherited pseudocholinesterase deficiency. He should not receive succinylcholine or mivacurium; other neuromuscular blockers and ester local anesthetics in usual doses are generally acceptable, with the anesthesia team informed. We recommend he carry a medical alert card or bracelet and tell every future anesthesia team. Blood relatives may wish to be tested.

We have spoken with Mr. Coughlin by phone and mailed him a letter and alert card.

Allergies/alerts updated in our record: succinylcholine (prolonged apnea).

Sincerely,
Department of Anesthesiology, regional hospital

documents.title: Anesthesia results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Brett, I got the anesthesia letter. The tests confirm what they suspected: you have an inherited form of pseudocholinesterase deficiency. Your body can't break down one specific paralytic drug (succinylcholine) normally, which is why you stayed paralyzed after surgery. It doesn't affect your day to day health at all. It matters only if you ever need anesthesia: anyone putting you to sleep needs to know so they use a different drug. I've put it at the top of your chart as a high-priority alert. Please wear a medical alert bracelet, and since it runs in families, your parents or any siblings could ask their doctors about testing.

documents.title: RE: Anesthesia results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. They called me too. Ordered a bracelet. Will tell my folks.

45M, 3 weeks s/p ORIF R femoral shaft fracture (12/02/2024). Doing well. Pain controlled, using oxycodone rarely. Ambulating with walker.

Exam: incision healed, staples removed, steri-strips applied. No erythema or drainage. Thigh soft. Knee flexion coming along. NVI distally.

Plan: WBAT, progress to cane as tolerated. Continue PT. Finish enoxaparin course. Return 4-5 weeks with X-rays. Off work for now.

Allergies: succinylcholine (prolonged apnea).

documents.body: Called pt. Finished enoxaparin 12/30, no problems. Stopped oxycodone-APAP about a week ago, using plain Tylenol after PT. Has leftover tabs - gave him drop-off info for the police station kiosk. Walking with a cane in the house now. PT 2x/week. Ortho f/u 1/27.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Brett is back at full duty since late March, ortho released him. Leg feels normal.

Interval: R femur ORIF 12/2024, healed. Pseudocholinesterase deficiency confirmed (homozygous atypical) after the succinylcholine event - wears the bracelet, showed me. Albumin 3.1 in Dec.

GI: taking enzymes faithfully, stools formed, no abdominal pain, no flares. Eating more protein, mostly shakes at lunch.
CV: no chest pain, no palpitations, no dyspnea on stairs or ladders.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine - prolonged paralysis (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).
SH: unchanged. Former smoker. Beers on weekends. Back on the motorcycle - we talked about gear.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight unchanged. Well appearing. HEENT normal, dentition fine. Neck no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, apical click and soft late systolic murmur same as before. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender. R thigh scar well healed, full strength. No edema. Skin ok.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - Tdap today. FIT kit given, he will mail it back this week. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. PHQ-9 2.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today.
3. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis - stable on enzymes. Gallbladder still in situ; he wants to get through the building season before thinking about surgery. Revisit in the fall.
4. MVP, mild MR - unchanged exam.
5. Pseudocholinesterase deficiency - documented as high-priority alert.
6. Obesity - stable.

RTC 2 months for a check on albumin and weight.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look good. Albumin up to 3.4 - still just under normal but heading the right way. Cholesterol and sugar normal, blood counts and liver tests normal. Keep doing what you're doing with the protein.

documents.title: FIT result

documents.body: Doc, been running fevers on and off for about 2 weeks, chills and soaking the sheets some nights. Wiped out by mid afternoon which isn't me. No cough no burning when I pee. Thought it was a summer bug but it's not going away. Had a tooth pulled a few weeks ago if that matters.

documents.title: RE: Fevers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It matters, given your valve. I want to see you Friday first thing, 7:30. If you get a fever over 102, shaking chills, chest pain or short of breath before then, go to the ED and text me.

documents.title: Same-day Visit - Fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M with MVP/mild MR here for ~2 wk of intermittent fevers, night sweats and fatigue. Dental extraction about 3 weeks ago. No cough, dysuria, diarrhea, rash, joint pain, travel. No IV drug use.

Exam: T 38.3, HR 100, otherwise vitals as charted. Tired, not toxic. Mouth: extraction site healed. Heart: there is a new holosystolic blowing murmur at the apex radiating into the axilla, clearly louder and longer than the soft late systolic murmur I have documented before. No rub. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No splinter hemorrhages or conjunctival petechiae that I can see. No edema.

A/P: Fever with a new regurgitant murmur after a dental extraction in a patient with MVP - endocarditis until proven otherwise. He needs blood cultures before any antibiotic and an echo today. Sent directly to the regional hospital ED, called ahead and spoke with the ED physician. No antibiotics given here. He is driving himself - discussed, he insists, it is 10 minutes.

results.text: Positive, 3 of 3 sets: viridans group streptococci. Penicillin MIC 0.06 mcg/mL (susceptible); ceftriaxone susceptible.

reports.text: Indication: fever, new murmur. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Mitral valve prolapse. A mobile echodensity consistent with vegetation is attached to the mitral valve. Mild mitral regurgitation. Aortic valve trileaflet, opens normally, no vegetation. Right heart normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Vegetation on the mitral valve consistent with infective endocarditis in the setting of mitral valve prolapse.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 08/01/2025.

CC: fevers x2 weeks, new murmur, sent in by PCP.

HPI: 46-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis from gallstones and a prolapsing mitral valve with mild MR, prior right femur ORIF, referred by his primary care physician after two weeks of on-and-off fevers, night sweats and fatigue, with a newly heard murmur. Had a tooth extracted about three weeks ago. No recent travel. Denies intravenous drug use.

PMH: as above; hypoalbuminemia; pseudocholinesterase deficiency.
Meds: pancrelipase with meals and snacks, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.
Allergies: succinylcholine (prolonged apnea).

Vitals: T 38.5 C, HR 102, BP 130/85.
Exam: dentition in good repair, no dental abscess or gum infection. Cardiac: high-pitched blowing systolic murmur loudest at the apex, radiating to the left axilla. Lungs clear. No peripheral stigmata noted.

Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250. ESR 45. Blood cultures x3 drawn before antibiotics.
Formal TTE: vegetation on the mitral valve.

MDM: presumed native mitral valve endocarditis after dental extraction. Cardiology and ID notified. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV given after cultures.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service
Admitted 08/01/2025, discharged 08/07/2025

Principal diagnosis: native mitral valve infective endocarditis, viridans group streptococci, following dental extraction.
Other: mitral valve prolapse with mild MR; chronic gallstone pancreatitis on enzymes; hypoalbuminemia; obesity; pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

Course: Admitted from ED with fever and a new apical murmur; TTE showed a mitral valve vegetation. All three admission blood culture sets grew viridans group streptococci, penicillin MIC 0.06. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h continued from the ED. Defervesced on hospital day 2. Surveillance cultures 08/03 no growth. Infectious disease and cardiology consulted; TEE not pursued given a diagnostic TTE and no clinical sign of perivalvular extension; no surgical indication identified. Dental evaluation found good oral hygiene with no ongoing source. Albumin 2.8 on 08/02. PICC placed 08/05 (right basilic) without complication.

Discharge plan: ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours through 08/28/2025 via home infusion; weekly CBC and BMP to ID clinic; ID clinic visit in about 2 weeks; repeat TTE at end of therapy with cardiology; PCP within one week.
Home medications unchanged: pancrelipase, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home since yesterday. Home infusion nurse came this morning, ceftriaxone running fine through PICC, he's been taught to flush. No fever since the hospital. Tired. PICC site clean, no arm swelling. Labs will be drawn Mondays by the infusion nurse. TCM visit Tue 8/12 confirmed. Work note requested - off through the end of antibiotics, PCP to sign.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after admission 8/1-8/7 for viridans strep mitral valve endocarditis (3/3 cultures, PCN MIC 0.06), sent in from here the day he presented. Repeat cultures 8/3 no growth. On ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily via R arm PICC through 8/28. ID following; echo again at end of therapy.

Feels better each day, sleeping through without sweats. Appetite coming back. Down about 3.5 kg from his usual. No fevers at home. No chest pain or breathlessness.

Meds: ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h (home infusion), Creon w/ meals and snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Looks less washed out. Heart regular, holosystolic apical murmur radiating to axilla, unchanged from 8/1. Lungs clear. PICC R upper arm clean, no tenderness, no arm swelling. No edema.

Labs 8/11 from home infusion: WBC now normal, renal function and potassium normal.

A/P:
1. Mitral valve IE on ceftriaxone - responding. Complete course 8/28. Weekly labs. ID f/u.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - 2.8 inpatient; will recheck after antibiotics are done.
3. Weight loss from the illness - expect it to come back.
4. Work - off through end of therapy, note signed.
5. Will talk about dental prophylaxis going forward once he is off IV antibiotics.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Clinic Note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious disease clinic, regional hospital. Visit 08/21/2025.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for following Mr. Coughlin with us. He is on day 21 of ceftriaxone for native mitral valve endocarditis due to viridans group streptococci (PCN MIC 0.06), after a dental extraction. Cultures cleared by 08/03.

He is afebrile and feels close to normal. No rash, no diarrhea. PICC site clean. Weekly labs reviewed and unremarkable.

Exam: well appearing. Apical systolic murmur radiating to the axilla. No embolic phenomena. No PICC site erythema.

Plan: complete ceftriaxone 2 g daily through 08/28/2025, then home infusion will pull the PICC after the final dose. End-of-therapy TTE with cardiology. He now meets criteria for antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures that manipulate gingiva, given prior endocarditis; we would suggest amoxicillin 2 g orally 30-60 minutes beforehand. No routine follow-up needed with us unless fever recurs.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

documents.title: Line out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last bag was the 28th, nurse pulled the PICC yesterday. Arm's fine. Can I go back to work Monday? Need a note for the company.

documents.title: RE: Line out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Yes, back Monday, full duty. Note attached. Take it a little easy the first week - your stamina will lag behind how you feel. Echo with cardiology is coming up in October.

medications.sig: Take 4 capsules (2 g) by mouth 30-60 minutes before dental procedures

documents.title: Dentist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Dentist wants to see me for a cleaning and says I need antibiotics first now? Is that right

documents.title: RE: Dentist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that's right now that you've had endocarditis. Before any dental work, including cleanings, take 4 amoxicillin capsules (2 grams total) 30 to 60 minutes before the appointment. I've sent a prescription to your pharmacy with refills so you always have a dose at home. Let the dentist know about the bracelet too, in case they ever sedate you.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 10/20/2025.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Coughlin, 46, after treatment of native mitral valve endocarditis (viridans streptococci, 4 weeks ceftriaxone ending 08/28/2025), on a background of mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation. His father has MVP as well.

He feels well. No dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or exertional limitation; back to supervising job sites.

Exam: BP and HR normal. Mid-systolic click with an apical systolic murmur radiating to the axilla. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: no residual vegetation; prolapse with mild MR; normal LV size and function.

Impression: endocarditis resolved. MVP with mild MR.
Recommendations: continue amoxicillin prophylaxis before dental procedures for life. Repeat echo in 2-3 years or sooner with symptoms. No restrictions. Return as needed.

Medications reviewed: pancrelipase, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit

documents.body:
Winter check-in, slow season at work. Feels fully back to himself after the endocarditis. Weight back to baseline. Cardiology echo 10/20 clean: no residual vegetation, MVP with mild MR, normal LV.

GI: on Creon with every meal/snack, omeprazole daily. No abdominal pain episodes. Stools fine.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine - pseudocholinesterase deficiency (homozygous atypical).

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender, no Murphy sign. No edema.

A/P:
1. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis, gallbladder in situ - the stones are what started this, and leaving the gallbladder in keeps the door open for more attacks. He is ready now. Referral to general surgery for elective lap chole. Will make sure anesthesia knows about the cholinesterase deficiency.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today.
3. MVP/mild MR, s/p mitral IE - stable, prophylaxis before dental work.
4. Obesity - weight back to baseline.

RTC April physical.

reports.text: Regional hospital imaging. Ordered by general surgery. Liver normal in size and echotexture, no focal lesion. Gallbladder contains multiple mobile shadowing gallstones. Gallbladder wall is not thickened; no pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy sign negative. Common bile duct normal in caliber. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas; visualized portions unremarkable. Right kidney normal.
reports.conclusion: Cholelithiasis without sonographic evidence of acute cholecystitis. Normal common bile duct caliber.

Outside general surgery practice. Visit 02/16/2026.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Mr. Coughlin, 46, with chronic pancreatitis attributed to gallstones, gallbladder still in place, on pancreatic enzyme replacement. Currently asymptomatic. Ultrasound 02/09 shows multiple gallstones with a normal wall and a normal-caliber duct.

History reviewed including mitral valve endocarditis in 2025 (treated, resolved), MVP with mild MR, and pseudocholinesterase deficiency with prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine in 2024.

Exam: obese abdomen, soft, nontender, no hernia. Healed right thigh incision.

Impression: cholelithiasis with gallstone-related chronic pancreatitis.
Plan: elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, booked 06/08/2026 at his request (around his work schedule). Preoperative evaluation with PCP within 30 days of surgery. Anesthesia preoperative clinic aware of the cholinesterase deficiency; succinylcholine will be avoided.

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy 6/8/2026, outside general surgery.

Functional capacity good: walks job sites and climbs ladders all day, more than 4 METs without symptoms. No chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, palpitations. No bleeding history. Only prior anesthetic was 12/2024 (femur fixation) complicated by prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine; workup showed homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

PMH: chronic gallstone pancreatitis on enzymes, MVP with mild MR, mitral valve endocarditis 2025 (viridans strep, treated, resolved on 10/2025 echo), hypoalbuminemia, obesity, R femur ORIF 2024. Former smoker.
Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: SUCCINYLCHOLINE - prolonged apnea (pseudocholinesterase deficiency). Also avoid mivacurium.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway: normal mouth opening, full neck range. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal.
Labs: CBC, BMP today.

Assessment: low-to-intermediate risk procedure, good functional capacity, no active cardiac condition. Acceptable to proceed.
Recommendations:
- Anesthesia: no succinylcholine or mivacurium. Letter to anesthesia and surgery sent with the 12/2024 cholinesterase report.
- Endocarditis prophylaxis is not indicated for this GI procedure.
- Aspirin: per surgeon.
- Continue Creon with meals once eating.

Copy to general surgery and anesthesia preoperative clinic.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery / Critical Care
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 06/08/2026, discharged 06/17/2026.

Procedure 06/08/2026: elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis with gallstone-related chronic pancreatitis. Completed without immediate complication. Anesthesia: known homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase deficiency; succinylcholine avoided, a non-depolarizing relaxant used and fully reversed before extubation.

Postoperative course: tachypnea and hypoxia developed after surgery; transferred to the ICU on postoperative day 1 (06/09). On ICU arrival afebrile, respiratory rate 28, SpO2 92% on room air, with crackles throughout both lung fields. POD 1 labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.5, platelets 250, creatinine 1.0, BNP 50. ABG pH 7.48, PaCO2 32, PaO2 70. Portable chest film: bilateral infiltrates. With normal BNP and normal LV function on prior echo, a cardiogenic cause was felt unlikely; diagnosis acute respiratory distress syndrome.

Oxygenation worsened over the day despite high-flow nasal oxygen and he was intubated the evening of 06/09. Lung-protective ventilation; worst PaO2/FiO2 108 on PEEP 14. Prone positioning was used. Cisatracurium infusion for 48 hours for ventilator synchrony (not dependent on plasma cholinesterase). Conservative fluid strategy. Blood and respiratory cultures negative. No clear precipitant was identified. Oxygenation improved steadily; extubated 06/13, transferred out of the ICU 06/14, weaned to room air, discharged home 06/17.

Pathology: cholelithiasis, chronic inflammation of the gallbladder wall, no dysplasia or malignancy.

Discharge diagnoses: ARDS after laparoscopic cholecystectomy, resolving; status post cholecystectomy; chronic pancreatitis; MVP with mild MR; history of mitral valve endocarditis (2025); pseudocholinesterase deficiency; hypoalbuminemia; obesity.
Discharge medications: pancrelipase with meals and snacks, aspirin 81 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily; amoxicillin before dental work as before.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; chest imaging in 4-6 weeks; pulmonology clinic. Surgery clinic 2 weeks for wound check.

Note: hospital course details from the critical care team are summarized above.

documents.title: Pulmonary Clinic Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Visit 07/27/2026.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Coughlin, 47, about seven weeks after ARDS that began the day after an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (intubated 06/09-06/13, prone positioning, no precipitant found, cultures negative). Former smoker, quit at 42.

He is improving steadily: walking two miles, still breathless on more than a flight of stairs, no cough, no chest pain, no orthopnea.

Exam: comfortable, room air saturation normal, lungs clear, no clubbing, no edema.
Chest X-ray 07/13: near-complete clearing.

Impression: ARDS, resolved, with expected recovery of exercise tolerance still under way.
Plan: graded return to activity; may return to work on light duty now, full duty in about a month if he keeps improving. Return to clinic in 3 months; sooner with any setback.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.
